answer: Fake identities can spread like a vine, so an agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days. The bond serves as an anchor: opening 1,000 accounts ties up $100,000, with financing costs even if every bond is returned. The market can harbor anonymous agents while making mass identity creation expensive; cryptographic proof that an agent signed conflicting delivery receipts triggers forfeiture of its bond.
